# Data & Methods

# Data Description
For this research, the dataset of the Michigan Residential Community Survey was used. This survey was used to evaluate the Michigan Learning Communities and focussed, among other things, on the social satisfaction of their first-year students. For the sake of this course, only the data of one of the programs was used, from the first cohort (2022-2023). The pre-survey (Wave 1) could be answered from October 19 to November 19 and the post-survey (Wave 2) could be answered from March 3th to April 10th. 

This specific program contained 121 students who answered at least one of these surveys. The response rate for the first wave was 91,474% and for the second wave it was 94,21%. Eleven students only answered the questions of the second wave and thirteen students only answered the questions of the first wave.

## Variables

### Hanging out
The reciprocated ties of the 'hanging out' variable are the dependent variable for the first hypothesis and an independent variable for the second and third hypothesis. The question asked for this variable was 'Which students in your MLC do you hang around with and talk to the most?'. Students could nominate up to ten of their fellow students. 

For the students that only participated in one of the two waves, it meant that if they were nominated by their fellow students anyways, this was still coded as a non-nomination (0), because they did not consent to participating in that specific wave. Additionally, their own nominations (which was an NA), were also coded as 0. This means that there could be some bias in the network structures. 

### Social satisfaction
Social satisfaction is the dependent variable for the second and third hypothesis. 

Five questions were asked to measure the social satisfaction of the students. As two of these questions were asked as a negative (I feel left out of things, I am lonely), only the three positive questions (I have made some good friends at the U of M, I am happy with my friends at the U of M, I like how my social life is going this year) were taken into account for the sake of this course. Answered were proposed on a scale from 1 (Strongly disagree) to 7 (Strongly agree). The average of these three positives was taken to measure the social satisfaction of students. 

## Covariate: Parental Education Level
Parental education level is one of the independent variables for the first and third hypothesis. Students had to answer what the highest education level was for both of their parents. For this study, these responses were first binary coded for both of the parents. If the highest education the parent had completed was 'trade/technical/vocational training' or less than this, the response was coded as 0, anything above that was coded as 1. Followingly, responses for parent 1 and parent 2 were taken together. If at least one of the parents had completed higher education, the variable was coded as 1 for the student. 

## Control covariates
To account for the influence of other factors on the hypotheses, gender and ethnicity were taken into account as control variables. 

# Methods
## Descriptives 
As my first research question is about whether segregation based on parental education level occurs on the macro-level, I will look at two relevant segregation statistics for this: Coleman's homophily index and Moran's I. Additionally, I am interested in reciprocity, so I will also look into what that looks like for both of the waves and I will also report how many mutual dyads have occurred. Lastly, for some basic descriptives, the number of ties will be reported, as well as the density of the network in both waves. 

## Explanatory
I have done the exploratory analyses by making use of the Stochastic Actor-Oriented Models (SAOMs) with RSiena [@ripley2025].These model the evolution of network structures and in this case, also the behaviour of the agents. It does this through estimating 'rules' for the agents on how they change their ties or behaviour. These rules can be seen as the micro theory of action. Into my RSiena model, structural effects, covariate effects and behavioural effects have been taken into account. For each hypothesis, there are a couple of effects that will be taken into account.

**Hypothesis 2** 
The second research question aims to estimate to what extent reciprocated friendships occur between students whose parents have the same educational level and whether this is significant. For this model, I include sameX and sameXRecip and because the underlying mechanisms for sameX are egoX and altX, these are included as well. 

*EgoX takes into account how many out-degrees ego sends and how this relates to the average amount of out-degrees that a node with the same covariate send out. AltX looks at how many of the actors that i has a tie to, have the same covariate.* SameX then looks at how many of the ties that i has send out to actors j, have exactly the same value on their covariate. So, in this case, SameX looks at if I send out a tie to for example, four people, how many of these people have parents with the same educational level as my parents? sameXRecip, followingly, then looks at how many of the reciprocated ties that i has, are with an actor that has the same covariate as them.
